messages:
maria: Hey team — need quick advice. We're onboarding an external analytics contractor (TempCorp) who needs to view application logs for debugging and run readonly SQL on the analytics project. We want least-privilege and logs must have PII redacted. Should I give them roles/logging.viewer + roles/bigquery.dataViewer at project scope, or create a custom role? Any short checklist? cc @security-bot

devon: I'd prefer a custom role scoped to the project. Built-in roles are convenient but often too broad. For logs specifically, grant the minimal logging permissions like logging.logEntries.list and avoid broad resourcemanager perms. For BigQuery give table read permissions only. Also ensure logs are redacted upstream. Example gcloud to create a small role below.

samir: quick question — can we time-limit access so it's not permanent? We shouldn't have a long-lived binding for a contractor.

security-bot: Recommended checklist: 1) Create custom role with explicit perms 2) Use conditional binding or issue short-lived credentials (JIT) 3) Ensure log redaction (ingest-time or sinks) 4) Add approval ticket and justification in access logs. If on GCP, IAM Conditions or temporary service-account tokens are the usual pattern.

devon: Example role creation (quick):

```
gcloud iam roles create temp_analytics_viewer \
  --project=redwood-analytics \
  --title="Temp Analytics Viewer" \
  --permissions=logging.logEntries.list,bigquery.tables.getData,bigquery.jobs.list \
  --stage=GA
```

devon: Then create a time-bounded policy binding instead of org-wide role:

```
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-analytics \
  --member="user:contractor@tempcorp.com" \
  --role="projects/redwood-analytics/roles/temp_analytics_viewer" \
  --condition='expression=request.time < timestamp("2025-01-10T00:00:00Z")'
```

samir: Nice. Who signs off on the PR for the custom role? @devon or @maria to own, but we should get one security reviewer.

maria: I'll create the role PR and an approval ticket in the access-management board with justification + expiry date. Will tag @security-bot for review.

security-bot: One more: double-check that logs with PII are redacted at ingestion or excluded. If you find PII in existing logs, do NOT grant access until it's remediated — escalate to SRE. Also add an audit entry referencing the ticket id.

maria: Got it. I'll pause bindings until redaction check is done and then follow the time-limited binding flow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
